findings.title: Uncapped 2% Daily Penalties on Total Contract Value
findings.deviation: LDs are 2% of Total Contract Value per day (vs 0.5% of milestone per week) and are uncapped and non-exclusive.
findings.impact: AtliQ could incur penalties exceeding the total project value for minor delays in a single milestone.
findings.quote: if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs where the delay is caused by the client; LDs are the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Unilateral Unlimited Liability for AtliQ
findings.deviation: AtliQ's liability is entirely uncapped for all claims, while the Client's liability is capped at fees paid.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces unlimited financial exposure for breaches, data incidents, and indemnities regardless of project size.
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.
findings.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim; carve-outs limited to fraud and wilful misconduct; data-protection liability under a separate super-cap.

findings.title: No Payment for Work in Progress
findings.deviation: Payment upon convenience termination is limited to previously accepted deliverables only.
findings.impact: AtliQ would lose the value of all labor and costs incurred for milestones currently in development at the time of termination.
findings.quote: Upon such termination, Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
findings.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs; mutual notice period.

findings.title: Assignment of Background IP and Tools
findings.deviation: The clause requires assignment of ownership (rather than a license) for any pre-existing materials used in deliverables.
findings.impact: AtliQ would lose ownership of its proprietary internal tools and software frameworks if they are incorporated into project deliverables.
findings.quote: Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein, including all intellectual property rights... [in] any Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into or necessary for the use of any Deliverable
findings.counterPosition: Client owns deliverables created specifically for it upon payment; AtliQ retains background IP and grants a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it as part of the deliverables.

findings.title: Indemnification for Client's Own Negligence
findings.deviation: AtliQ must indemnify the Client even if the loss was caused by the Client's own negligence.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be forced to pay for damages and legal fees resulting from errors or negligence committed by the Client's staff.
findings.quote: Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client... in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence.

findings.title: Commitment to $5M Cyber Insurance Limit
findings.deviation: Requires $5M in cyber liability coverage, exceeding AtliQ's current $1M limit.
findings.impact: AtliQ would be in immediate breach of contract upon signing unless it obtains significantly higher insurance coverage.
findings.quote: Contractor shall maintain... (c) cyber liability of $5,000,000 per claim;
findings.counterPosition: Align required limits with current cover ($1M), or agree a timeline and cost to increase cover before signature.

findings.title: Cross-Agreement Set-off Rights
findings.deviation: Allows the Client to withhold payment based on disputes in entirely unrelated agreements.
findings.impact: The client could stop paying for current project work because of a disagreement on a different contract.
findings.quote: Client may set off against any amount owed to Contractor any amount owed by Contractor to Client under this Agreement or any other agreement.
findings.counterPosition: Set-off limited to undisputed amounts under this agreement.

findings.title: 90-Day Invoice Submission Waiver
findings.deviation: AtliQ waives its right to payment if an invoice is not submitted within 90 days of acceptance.
findings.impact: Administrative delays in billing could result in the total forfeiture of fees for work already performed and accepted.
findings.quote: Invoices not submitted within ninety (90) days after acceptance shall be deemed waived.
findings.counterPosition: Remove the waiver clause; AtliQ should be paid for all work performed and accepted.

findings.title: No Deemed Acceptance Mechanism
findings.deviation: Prevents acceptance from occurring through use, payment, or the passage of time.
findings.impact: Milestones could remain technically 'unaccepted' indefinitely, delaying final payment even if the software is in live use.
findings.quote: Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use in production, by payment, or by the passage of time.
findings.counterPosition: Deliverables are deemed accepted if the client fails to provide a rejection notice within a defined period (e.g., 10 business days) or puts the deliverable into production use.

fine.note: Confidentiality obligations are mutual in substance and standard in scope.
The agreement is non-exclusive and contains no non-compete or non-solicit restrictions.
Offshore restrictions and security requirements are standard for a BAA-governed healthcare contract.
